title: Preparation of genetically engineered murine SINE RNA without endotoxin contamination
author: Liu, Lv, et al.
materials: Material•Triton X-114•3 mol/L sodium acetate (pH 6.0)•Absolute ethyl alcohol and 75% ethanol•10% SDS•Water-saturated phenol•Chloroform•Thermostatic metal bath•Shaker•High speed freezing centrifuge

steps.title: Transform and grow bacteria
steps.instruction: Transform 0.1–0.2 ml DE3 competent cells with 1 µl pET‑B1as vector (0.1 µg µl⁻¹); plate on LB agar containing 30 µg ml⁻¹ kanamycin (1.3 % agar) and incubate overnight. Pick 10–20 single colonies, wash with LB medium (30 µg ml⁻¹ kanamycin). Inoculate six 500 ml Erlenmeyer flasks each containing 200 ml LB (30 µg ml⁻¹ kanamycin). Shake at 120 rpm, 37 °C for ~3 h until OD₆₀₀ = 1.0. Add 2 ml 20 mg ml⁻¹ IPTG stock to each flask, shake another 2 h to induce B1as RNA. Harvest cells by centrifugation at 10 000 rpm for 5 min at 4 °C in 50 ml pointed‑bottom tubes; discard supernatant. Repeat centrifugation for the remaining culture. Expected yield ≈0.5 g wet cells per 200 ml culture.

steps.title: Extract RNA by SDS‑NaCl filtration
steps.instruction: Resuspend each cell pellet in normal saline (0.9 % NaCl) to obtain a 50 % (v/v) bacterial suspension (adjust volume with saline). Aliquot 1 ml of this suspension into a 50 ml tube, add 20 µl 50 mg ml⁻¹ lysozyme, and place on ice for 5 min to lyse. Add 9 ml 1.5 % SDS solution (final SDS ≈0.7 %), 6 µl DEPC, and 10 ml 4 M NaCl; mix gently. Filter the lysate through 10–15 µm slow‑filter paper at 4 °C. Precipitate the filtrate with three volumes of absolute ethanol at room temperature for 30 min, then centrifuge at 10 000 rpm for 10 min. Wash the pellet twice with 75 % ethanol, and dry the RNA pellet using hot air from a hair dryer (do not air‑dry). Prepare 2 ml of 0.5× DNase I digestion solution: 1.775 ml double‑distilled water, 0.1 ml 10× DNase I buffer, 0.1 ml RNase‑free DNase I (1 U ml⁻¹), and 25 µl RNase inhibitor (40 U ml⁻¹) (final DNase I 0.05 U ml⁻¹, inhibitor 0.5 U ml⁻¹). Add this solution to the dried RNA, incubate 30 min at 37 °C, then centrifuge 10 000 rpm for 10 min and collect the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: If no further endotoxin removal is required, treat the DNase I supernatant with the SDS hot‑phenol method to eliminate residual proteins and degraded DNA.

Optional Triton X‑114 cleanup (if additional endotoxin removal is desired): take 0.1 ml of the DNase I supernatant, perform SDS hot‑phenol extraction (add 0.1 vol 10 % SDS, 0.5 vol water‑saturated phenol, incubate 30 min at 60 °C; cool, add 0.25 vol chloroform, invert, centrifuge 10 000 rpm 10 min). Precipitate the resulting supernatant with three volumes of absolute ethanol at 4 °C for 30 min, centrifuge 10 000 rpm 10 min, wash twice with 75 % ethanol, dry with hot air, resuspend in DDW, measure OD260/280 and concentration, and adjust the remaining DNase I supernatant to 1 mg ml⁻¹ RNA using 0.5× DNase I buffer.

steps.title: Remove endotoxin by Triton X‑114
steps.instruction: To the 1 mg ml⁻¹ RNA solution add 0.1 vol 3 M sodium acetate (pH 6.0), then add 0.033 vol Triton X‑114 and mix. Shake the mixture at room temperature for 20 min, then incubate in a metal bath at 50 °C for 10 min. Allow to cool at room temperature for 5 min. Centrifuge at 10 000 rpm for 10 min at 23 °C using a high‑speed freezing centrifuge and collect the supernatant. Perform SDS hot‑phenol cleanup on the supernatant (add 0.1 vol 10 % SDS, 0.5 vol water‑saturated phenol, incubate 30 min at 60 °C; cool, add 0.25 vol chloroform, invert, centrifuge 10 000 rpm 10 min). Precipitate the cleaned supernatant with three volumes of absolute ethanol for 30 min at 4 °C, centrifuge 10 min at 10 000 rpm, wash the pellet twice with 75 % ethanol, and dry with hot air to obtain endotoxin‑free RNA.
